findings.title: Date-override hit returns available and skips busy times
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable returns true as soon as any date override is considered to cover the slot (the dateOverrideExist branch around line 133), before the busy-interval loop. Busy times from calendars and existing bookings are the only conflict filter applied to slots generated from working hours, and this function is that filter. It runs for every fixed host, which includes ordinary 1:1 and collective events (non-round-robin users are marked isFixed), and again for round-robin non-fixed hosts. On any day a host has a date override, slots during meetings are shown as free and can be double-booked.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects split schedules and ignores duration
findings.body: The new working-hours gate uses workingHours.find and treats a match as "outside hours" (lines 139-150). The callback returns true when the slot's UTC weekday is in an entry and the slot start is outside that one range. find therefore succeeds if any same-day window does not contain the slot. A normal lunch-break schedule (two rows such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same weekdays) rejects every slot, because each slot misses at least one window. This runs for all fixed hosts, including 1:1 events, so those users see no bookable times. The end minute is also copied from the slot start (line 142 uses slotStartTime for both start and end) instead of the slot end, so event length is never compared to the window end and a round-robin slot taken from a longer host can run past the fixed host's hours. A weekday with no matching entry is not rejected at all, so a fixed host with no hours that day is treated as free when the slot came from someone else.

findings.title: Override containment is inverted for multiple ranges
findings.body: Date overrides are scanned with find (lines 106-130), and a truthy callback is treated as "slot is not within the override", which makes checkIfIsAvailable return false. The callback returns true when the slot is outside a single range (ends at or before that range's start, or starts after that range's end). Two override windows on the same day, which is how a break is stored, therefore disqualify every slot: each slot is outside at least one range, so the fixed host has no availability that day. A slot is also treated as inside a range unless it is completely before or completely after it, so a slot that only partially overlaps (starts before the window and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it) is accepted and can extend past the override. The all-day block on line 114 compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds, so a zero-length override is not reliably treated as an all-day block.

findings.title: Override timezone shift keeps only clock time and can wipe the day
findings.body: The new conversion adds inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset to the override instants and then stores only .hour() and .minute() (lines 219-223). Those minutes are applied to whichever invitee day contains the unadjusted override.start (the filter at lines 206-208), not the day of the shifted time. When the offset crosses midnight, the clock wraps onto the wrong day. Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata, override stored as 02:00Z-04:00Z meaning 02:00-04:00 local, attendee in UTC. The offset is -330 minutes, hour() becomes 20:30, and that is added to the UTC day of 02:00Z, so slots show at 20:30Z the same date instead of 20:30Z the previous day. If only the start wraps, startTime exceeds endTime. Organizer IST 09:00-18:00 viewed from America/New_York (offset -630 minutes) becomes start 22:30 and end 07:30. buildSlots drops any range with start >= end (line 68), but the override block has already removed that user's normal working hours (lines 228-245), so the attendee sees no slots on the override day.

findings.title: Converted override minutes are shifted again for DST
findings.body: Override bounds are converted to invitee-local minutes using utcOffset() of the override's own date (lines 212-223). buildSlots then runs every slot, including those override minutes, through getTime, which adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff (lines 102-110). That term corrects working hours that were converted with today's offset rather than the booking date's offset. Override minutes are already based on the booking date, so the extra term moves them whenever today's DST offset differs from the booking day's and the organizer and invitee are not on the same DST schedule. Example: organizer America/New_York, attendee in UTC, today in July (EDT, utcOffset -240) and the booking in January (EST, utcOffset -300). organizerDSTDiff is 60 and inviteeDSTDiff is 0, so every override slot is shown one hour late. Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka have no DST, so the new test does not catch this.

findings.title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates
findings.body: Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by comparing formatted calendar dates (lines 110-111). slotStartTime is time.utc(), so its format() is the UTC date. The override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") with no .utc(), so format() uses the Node process timezone. On any server whose TZ is not UTC, an adjusted override whose UTC date differs from the server-local date will not match the slot, and the fixed-host override is ignored or applied to the wrong day. Example: server in America/Los_Angeles, override adjusted to 02:00 UTC formats as the previous local evening while the slot formats as the UTC date. The check this PR adds then does not run.

findings.title: Tests miss fixed-host overrides and timezone day boundaries
findings.body: The only new assertion re-fetches a personal-event date override with the attendee in Asia/Dhaka (+6) instead of Asia/Kolkata (+5:30) and expects the same UTC slot list. A 30-minute offset does not cross midnight or a DST change, so it does not catch override slots landing on the wrong day, ranges with start after end being dropped, or the extra DST shift in getTime. There is no round-robin case with a fixed host and a date override, which is the behavior the PR says it fixes, and no case where an override day also has a booking or calendar busy time. createBookingScenario never installs the hosts/isFixed rows, so the new checkIfIsAvailable branches are not exercised and the double-book and split-window regressions would not fail CI.
